html:
An explosive made by soaking nitroglycerin into a porous earth and packing it in sticks, patented by the Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel in 1867.

Nitroglycerin, discovered in 1847, was far stronger than gunpowder but so unstable that a jolt could set it off. Nobel's family made it in Sweden, and in 1864 an explosion at their works killed his younger brother Emil. Nobel looked for a way to tame it and found that mixing it with a fine clay like earth made a paste that was safe to handle and could be set off with a blasting cap he had also designed.

Dynamite changed mining, quarrying and building. It blasted the tunnels, cuttings and harbours of the railway age, from the Alps to the American West. It also went into weapons and was used by anarchist bombers.

Nobel grew rich from factories in many countries and from his brothers' oil company, Branobel, in Baku. In his will he left most of his fortune to fund the Nobel Prizes, first awarded in 1901.
sum: An explosive made by soaking nitroglycerin into a porous earth and packing it in sticks, patented by the Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel in 1867.
